title: introduce-token-warmup-envelope-and-burst-aware-alert-attenuator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Add a lightweight 'warmup envelope' abstraction and a burst-aware alert attenuator to reduce noisy alerts originating from initial-token burst behavior and short lived invocation spikes. Motivation: customer transports and some SDKs emit heavy prompt tokens at connection/handshake time (prefix warmup), which inflates per-invocation token cost/latency metrics for the first few tokens and produces long-tail alert noise. The warmup envelope estimates an invocation-specific initial token envelope (p50/p95 latency and cost) and exposes a smoothed metric that downstream alerting and dashboards can opt into. The burst-aware alert attenuator uses the envelope and short-window burst detectors to temporarily lower alert sensitivity for routes that show reproducible warmup characteristics. What this PR changes (high-level): - Telemetry ingestion: add envelope estimator and per-invocation warmup tag (telemetry/envelope_detector.go, ingest/processor/envelope_processor.py) - Tracing: mark spans for 'warmup_phase' and include envelope metadata (span attributes) - Metrics: expose token_warmup_envelope_p50/p95 and token_warmup_smoothed_cost_{route,tenant} - Alerts: add a default attenuator rule and introduce per-route opt-out labels (observability/alerts/burst_attenuator.rules) - Dashboards: new Warmup Envelope Explorer and a comparison panel showing raw vs smoothed cost - SDK: small helper to annotate warmup windows for self-hosted clients (sdk/python/redwood/observability.py) - Docs: docs/observability/warmup_envelope.md Motivation/Design notes: - Envelope is computed per-invocation using a short sliding window (configurable, default 8 tokens) and reports p50/p95; it is stored as a short-lived rollup on the ingestion path to avoid extra storage costs. - The smoothed metric subtracts the envelope from raw per-invocation cost/latency for the first N tokens to produce a corrected series that is more representative for SLOs. - Burst attenuator rules use the envelope and a burstiness score (ratio of first-window p95 to steady-state p95). For short-lived bursts (configurable TTL 30s) alerts are attenuated by increasing their threshold delta; this is a conservative change and opt-in per-route via labels is supported. Checklist: - [x] Envelope estimator implementation (telemetry service) - [x] Trace instrumentation (span attribute warmup_phase) - [x] Smoothed metric exposure and aggregation rollup - [x] Grafana panels + example dashboard - [x] Alert rule and attenuation logic + unit tests - [x] SDK helper and docs - [x] Integration test in CI (telemetry_integration.yml) Commits (summary): - Add envelope estimator and processor (initial implementation + unit tests) - Expose new metrics for envelope p50/p95 and smoothed cost - Trace attribute plumbing and SDK annotation helper - Add Grafana dashboard JSONNet with Warmup Envelope Explorer panels - Implement burst-aware attenuation rules and runtime config - Tests: unit + integration + CI wiring - Fix: reduce memory allocation in envelope bucketization (follow-up) Files changed (high-level): - telemetry/envelope_detector.go: core estimator and configuration
- telemetry/envelope_detector_test.go: unit tests for edge cases
- ingest/processor/envelope_processor.py: ingestion-side bucketizer and short-lived rollup emitter
- observability/dashboards/warmup_envelope.jsonnet: new dashboard panels and templating
- observability/alerts/burst_attenuator.rules: Prometheus/alertmanager attenuation rule scaffolding
- sdk/python/redwood/observability.py: helper to mark warmup windows from client-side SDKs
- docs/observability/warmup_envelope.md: design doc and rollout playbook
- ci/telemetry_integration.yml: adds an integration job that runs a small synthetic workload and validates envelope outputs
- examples/warmup-integration/README.md: how to reproduce with the local harness
- telemetry/rollup_config.yaml: rollup TTL and envelope window defaults
- tests/integration/test_warmup_envelope.py: CI integration test and synthetic workload generator
- scripts/dev/plot_warmup_envelope.py: developer helper for visualization Review conversation (highlights): - Samir Gupta (2026-02-15): "Nice work — can you quantify CPU/memory overhead on high-throughput ingestion? We should avoid per-invocation heavy allocations." Reply (Maya): "Benchmarked on a 1M RPS trace simulant — envelope extraction is ~0.7% CPU at default window 8. Follow-up commit reduces allocations further by reusing buckets; numbers included in telemetry/envelope_detector_test.go." - Lena Ortiz (2026-02-16): "How do we prevent gaming? If a client intentionally pads the first tokens, will this silence legitimate alerts?" Reply (Maya): "We added heuristics: envelope requires minimum steady-state length (configurable default 32 tokens) before attenuating alerts; the route-level opt-out label still exists for teams that want raw signals." - Priya Menon (2026-02-18): "Pls add an e2e integration in CI that asserts smoothed metrics are within expected bounds for the synthetic harness." Reply (Maya): "Added tests/integration/test_warmup_envelope.py and CI job; adjusted rollup TTL to keep short-lived state for the integration window." CI: - build: pass - unit tests: pass - integration (telemetry_integration): pass (job added, runs on merge) - lint: pass - flake8 (initial run): fail (line-length) -> fixed in follow-up commit Merge outcome: merged via squash-merge on 2026-02-20 by Maya Chen Additional notes and rollout plan: - Default attenuation is enabled for all routes, but attenuation magnitude is small by default; SRE will watch the Warmup Envelope Explorer for 2 weeks and evaluate any missed alerts. - Ops runbook included in docs/observability/warmup_envelope.md describing how to disable or tune envelope parameters per-route. - Release notes (brief): "Introduce warmup envelope estimation and burst-aware alert attenuation to reduce alert noise from initial-token bursts; new dashboard and opt-out labels."
